competencies.text: Apply best practices for handling, storage, and disposal of chemicals.
Create a table showing saltwater/wastewater effects on local ecosystems and recommend minimization strategies.

days.title: Safety First — Handling Chemicals
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to identify GHS hazard symbols, describe safe handling, storage, and disposal practices for household and laboratory chemicals, and explain the effects of saltwater/wastewater on local ecosystems.

🦺 Why Chemical Safety Matters

Every year in the Philippines, thousands of household accidents happen due to improper chemical handling. Common causes include:

  • Mixing incompatible chemicals (e.g., bleach + ammonia → toxic chloramine gas)
  • Storing chemicals in food containers (children mistake them for drinks)
  • Pouring chemicals down the drain (pollutes rivers and groundwater)
  • Ignoring warning labels

⚠️ GHS Hazard Symbols

The Globally Harmonized System (GHS) uses standardized pictograms to warn users about chemical hazards:

SymbolMeaningExample Product
💀 Skull & crossbonesAcute toxicity — can cause death or serious harmPesticides, rat poison
🔥 FlameFlammable — easily catches fireAlcohol, LPG, paint thinner
💥 Exploding bombExplosive or self-reactiveFirecrackers, some fertilizers
🧪 CorrosionCorrodes skin/metalsBleach, drain cleaner, muriatic acid
⚠️ Exclamation markIrritant — skin, eye, or respiratory irritationDetergent, shampoo, some cleaners
🌫️ Gas cylinderCompressed gas under pressureLPG tank, oxygen tank
🏥 Health hazardLong-term health effects (cancer, organ damage)Pesticides, some solvents
🌍 EnvironmentHazardous to aquatic lifeDetergent, motor oil, pesticides

🏠 Best Practices — Handling

  • Read the label before use — every time.
  • Wear gloves and, if needed, a mask.
  • Work in a well-ventilated area.
  • Never mix chemicals unless the label says it's safe.
  • Keep chemicals away from food and children.
  • Wash hands thoroughly after use.

📦 Best Practices — Storage

  • Store in original containers with labels intact.
  • Keep away from heat, sunlight, and open flames.
  • Store acids and bases separately (they react violently).
  • Store flammable liquids in a cool, dry, locked cabinet.
  • Keep out of reach of children and pets.

♻️ Best Practices — Disposal

  • Never pour chemicals down the sink, toilet, or storm drain.
  • Follow DENR guidelines and local barangay rules for hazardous waste.
  • Neutralize acids and bases before disposal when safe and instructed.
  • Take expired chemicals to designated hazardous waste collection points.
  • Recycle containers where possible.

🌊 Wastewater and Saltwater Effects on Ecosystems

Type of PollutionSourceEffect on Ecosystem
Saltwater intrusionOver-pumping of wells, sea-level riseSoil becomes too salty; crops fail; freshwater fish die; drinking water becomes undrinkable
Detergent wastewaterHousehold laundry, car washPhosphates cause algal blooms → fish kills (eutrophication)
Industrial wastewaterFactories, miningHeavy metals poison fish; destroy coral reefs; contaminate groundwater
Agricultural runoffFertilizers, pesticidesNutrient overload; pesticide bioaccumulation in fish; destruction of mangroves
Untreated sewageHouseholds without septic systemsBacterial contamination; disease outbreaks; oxygen depletion in rivers

💡 Minimization Strategies

  • Reduce: Buy only the amount of chemical you need.
  • Reuse: Refill containers at refilling stations (e.g., liquid soap).
  • Replace: Choose eco-friendly products (phosphate-free detergent, natural cleaners like vinegar + baking soda).
  • Recycle: Properly empty and recycle plastic containers.
  • Dispose responsibly: Use barangay hazardous waste collection events.

🇵🇭 Philippine Laws & Agencies

  • RA 6969 — Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act: Regulates import, manufacture, and disposal of toxic substances.
  • RA 9003 — Ecological Solid Waste Management Act: Mandates proper waste segregation and disposal.
  • DENR: Enforces environmental regulations and provides guidance on chemical disposal.
  • DOH: Monitors public health effects of chemical exposure.

📌 Quick Check

  • What does the skull-and-crossbones GHS symbol mean? (Answer: acute toxicity — can cause death or serious harm)
  • Why should you store acids and bases separately? (Answer: they can react violently if they touch)
  • What law regulates toxic substances in the Philippines? (Answer: RA 6969)

days.title: Match Game — Safety Symbols
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each GHS hazard symbol, safety practice, or wastewater type to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Acute toxicity — can cause death or serious harm
Corrodes skin or metals — like bleach or muriatic acid
Irritant to skin, eyes, or respiratory system
Hazardous to aquatic life — like detergents and motor oil
Seawater seeping into freshwater aquifers; causes crops to fail
Algal blooms caused by phosphate-rich wastewater; kills fish
Philippine law regulating toxic substances and hazardous waste

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Wastewater in the Community
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🏠 A household has several expired bottles of muriatic acid, bleach, and pesticides. What is the BEST way to dispose of them?

choices.label: A) Pour them down the kitchen sink
B) Take them to a designated barangay or DENR hazardous waste collection event
C) Throw them in the regular trash bin
D) Bury them in the backyard

scenario.text: 🌊 A coastal barangay notices that their wells are becoming salty, and rice farms are failing. What is the LIKELY cause?

choices.label: A) Saltwater intrusion from over-pumping groundwater and rising sea levels
B) Too much rainfall
C) Farmers adding too much fertilizer
D) Fish farming in the area

scenario.text: 🐟 A river near your barangay has turned green with algae and dead fish are washing ashore. Which cause is MOST likely?

choices.label: A) Household detergent wastewater containing phosphates, causing eutrophication
B) Too much rain
C) The fish migrated elsewhere
D) Local fishing activities

scenario.text: ⚠️ Your helper wants to clean the bathroom with bleach and then with an ammonia-based glass cleaner in the same session. What should you tell her?

choices.label: A) Never mix them — the combination releases toxic chloramine gas that can damage lungs
B) It's fine, they are both cleaners
C) Mix them to make a stronger cleaner
D) Use them together with warm water to activate the smell

scenario.text: 🏭 A factory discharges untreated chemical wastewater into the local river. Which Philippine law does this violate?

choices.label: A) RA 6969 (Toxic Substances and Hazardous Waste Control Act)
B) RA 9003 only
C) No law is violated

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Safety Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Safety Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What does the GHS skull-and-crossbones symbol mean?

choices.label: A) Acute toxicity — can cause death or serious harm
B) Flammable liquid
C) Corrosive to metals
D) Harmless

escape.text: Why must acids and bases be stored separately?

choices.label: A) They can react violently if they touch
B) They have different colors
C) They smell different
D) They weigh differently

escape.text: What is the BEST practice when handling chemicals at home?

choices.label: A) Wear gloves, work in a well-ventilated area, and read the label
B) Work in a closed room to avoid drafts
C) Mix all cleaners to save time
D) Store them in food containers for easy access
A) Algal blooms caused by excess nutrients (phosphates) in water — kills fish
B) A cleaning process
C) A form of distillation
D) A method of water purification

escape.text: Which Philippine law specifically regulates toxic substances and hazardous waste?
What is the BEST way to dispose of leftover household chemicals?

choices.label: A) Take them to a designated hazardous waste collection point following DENR guidelines
B) Pour them into the storm drain
C) Throw them in the regular trash
D) Bury them in the backyard
